sections.heading: 1. Talk it through
lines: ① Mention any sore or sensitive spots first.
② Breathe out slowly as pressure goes on.
③ Say "lighter" any time, no need to tough it out.

sections.heading: 2. Get checked first if…
lines: An area feels warm, puffy or very sore,
or pain spreads — see a physio or GP.

caption:
Momo loves a massage, but she always wonders what her therapist's hands are actually looking for.

Remedial massage therapists feel for how soft, firm or guarded muscles are, where the tender spots sit and how you react to pressure, often comparing one side with the other. It's useful information, but it isn't a diagnosis.

Speak up about pressure any time. Your feedback matters as much as their hands. Warmth, swelling or pain that spreads is a reason to see a physio or GP first.

Our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physio are happy to explain as they go. Book online via the link in bio 🐱

General information only — not a substitute for an individual assessment.
